scenario: [LDTL.4.1]: the engine evaluates an `emit`'s `retain:` expression only after every slot value of the action, so where a slot value and `retain:` would both fault, the fault recorded is the slot value's and `retain:` is not evaluated. `dynamic_ttl` is on, and `Out` is `scope ttl 1_h` with no `ts`. Three rules, each taking one `Trig` by its key, so each fault is at its own (node, rule) site and none is latched away ([LERR.9.5]). Each writes `q: t.a // t.b`, an Int floor division that traps DIVIDE_BY_ZERO when `b` is 0 ([LEXP.7.15.1]), and `retain: t.f::Int * 1_s`, whose cast traps NOT_REPRESENTABLE when `f` is 1e300 ([LCST.4.5.4]), a different kind. Both faulting (`b` = 0, `f` = 1e300) gives the slot's DIVIDE_BY_ZERO; only `retain:` faulting (`b` = 1) gives NOT_REPRESENTABLE; only the slot faulting (`f` = 1.0) gives DIVIDE_BY_ZERO. One assert and one pump per case, so the log order is the steps' order. `faulted` logs each ComputationError's rule and kind ([LERR.9.2]); `leaked` logs any `Out` and must never fire, because every emit here faults. A runtime that evaluates `retain:` first logs `emit_both NOT_REPRESENTABLE`. PATH PINNED: libds `rete/engine.c`'s `emit` path, whose `ttl_override` follows its assigns; the Mercury runtime's `ds.exec.assert_verb`, whose `assign_fault` evaluates the assigns and then the override.
rules_ds:
use default:
    dynamic_ttl: true

schema Trig scope logical:
    k: Int key
    a: Int mutable
    b: Int mutable
    f: Float mutable

schema Out scope ttl 1_h:
    k: Int
    q: Int

rule emit_both:
    Trig t where t.k == 1
->
    emit Out k: t.k
        q: t.a // t.b
        retain: t.f::Int * 1_s

rule emit_retain:
    Trig t where t.k == 2
->
    emit Out k: t.k
        q: t.a // t.b
        retain: t.f::Int * 1_s

rule emit_slot:
    Trig t where t.k == 3
->
    emit Out k: t.k
        q: t.a // t.b
        retain: t.f::Int * 1_s

rule faulted:
    ComputationError c
->
    log info "{c.rule} {c.kind}"

rule leaked:
    Out
->
    log info "leaked"
